description: Build a living ecosystem in Rust, and understand the rules that shape it.

modules.title: A tick is a promise
modules.summary: Follow one reserve through a tick, then separate the world's state from the way it is drawn.

modules.title: Who owns the next change?
modules.summary: Predict which value changes when you move, copy, or borrow it. Make the compiler part of the experiment.

modules.title: Ask the world a typed question
modules.summary: Use a query signature to say which entities matter and which data the system may change.

modules.title: Give the number a unit
modules.summary: Separate a requested cost, an actual payment, and the reserve left. Let types and boundary tests keep the distinction visible.

modules.title: Missing is a different state
modules.summary: Describe an absent choice, an unresolved identity, and a present zero without turning them into the same result.

modules.title: A rejected request has a reason
modules.summary: Carry a form input through parsing and domain validation. Return a useful error instead of a misleading default.

modules.title: Put the boundary in the code
modules.summary: Give callers an honest public interface while keeping construction rules close to the values they protect.

modules.title: Collect a report, release the world
modules.summary: Turn borrowed observations into owned report rows, with explicit ordering and honest missing data.

modules.title: A trait is a promise you can use
modules.summary: Give identities meaningful comparison and reporting capabilities, then let a generic function state the capability it needs.

modules.title: Prove that the borrows cannot meet
modules.summary: Make read and write sets explicit, then use a dual-role entity to test the boundary.

modules.title: Give the observations an order
modules.summary: Bracket one real mutation with two observations. Explain how identical final values can hide different execution histories.

modules.title: Change structure at a known boundary
modules.summary: Follow a queued row across an explicit application point, then retain an observation after its entity is gone.

modules.title: Make a test disagree with a plausible mistake
modules.summary: Separate a correct helper from correct selection, schedule wiring, and the value an observer actually saw.

modules.title: Connect one affordable action to the world
modules.summary: Return to the canonical learner-owned movement task and connect its one edit to a reviewed, visible consequence.

modules.title: A finite meal has two sides
modules.summary: Resolve two consumers against one finite patch and keep requested intake separate from actual gain.

modules.title: Choose, then revalidate a target
modules.summary: Choose from a bounded snapshot, then check the live target again before committing a meal.

modules.title: Compare individuals fairly
modules.summary: Give individuals different costs while holding the starting conditions fixed, then separate that comparison from a density change.

modules.title: Let environmental input change supply
modules.summary: Trace lit and dark ticks and show how the selected growth-and-meal order changes a patch at capacity.

modules.title: Keep a disappearance explainable
modules.summary: Record one terminal transition and distinguish a complete zero count from history that no longer covers the question.

modules.title: Consume once, even before removal
modules.summary: Let two hunters compete for one prey and make its immediate availability authoritative before deferred despawn.

modules.title: Make rest a commitment you can inspect
modules.summary: Keep fatigue separate from energy and compare a reactive choice with an activity that lasts for a stated number of ticks.

modules.title: Commit both parents before creating a child
modules.summary: Validate and charge a pair atomically, then give a deferred newborn an explicit first action boundary.

modules.title: Keep inheritance distinct from selection
modules.summary: Copy and vary an offspring trait while preserving parents, units, identity, and enough provenance to replay the proposal.

modules.title: Make a comparison explain its denominator
modules.summary: Compare a declared intervention across matched cohorts, retaining losses and missing coverage in the report.

modules.title: Let a view borrow exactly what it needs
modules.summary: Relate a journal view to its actual owner without tying it to a temporary search term.

modules.title: Choose the owner before the abstraction
modules.summary: Compare concrete report formats with dynamic dispatch and distinguish shared ownership from permission to mutate.

modules.title: Accept asynchronous results at a tick boundary
modules.summary: Let native workers finish out of order while run and request identities keep stale work out of the authoritative tick.

modules.title: Read the code a macro asks Rust to check
modules.summary: Build a small diagnostic assertion, inspect what it expands into, and keep functions and concrete types as the default.
